title: Trenholm agitated before jail death: guards
article: The coroner's inquest looking into the death of a Port Elgin, N.B., man has been told he was pacing and drinking a lot of water in an RCMP lockup during the hours before he died.
Randy Nelson Trenholm, 50, died after a night in custody at the Shediac RCMP station in June 2007.

Guard Richard Leblanc testified that he came on duty at 8:30 p.m. on June 1 and noticed right away that something was strange about Trenholm's behaviour. Trenholm was pacing and drinking a lot of water, and told him that he was claustrophobic.
Because Trenholm wouldn't sleep, Leblanc said he turned the heat up to make him drowsy - a practice he said he had heard about from police officers. But it didn't work.

Guard Jean-Maurice Leblanc said that when he came on duty at 2 a.m. on June 2, he saw Trenholm pacing and trying to vomit twice. Later, the guard said, he saw Trenholm banging his head against a wall. At 6 a.m. he called an ambulance when he noticed Trenholm was shaking.

Jean-Maurice Leblanc testified that paramedics said Trenholm's vital signs were OK and gave him a form to sign saying Trenholm had refused medical care. The guard told the inquest he shouldn't have signed this form because he didn't know if that was true.
At 8:40 a.m., he saw Trenholm shaking, with foam and blood coming out of his mouth.
The ambulance was called again, but Trenholm was pronounced dead on arrival at the Dr. Georges-L.-Dumont Hospital in Moncton.
The inquest has heard that the video monitoring system in the jail failed to record images that night.
On Monday, Coroner John Evans told the four-man, one-woman jury in Moncton that Trenholm was an alcoholic who had been on a three-week binge when he was arrested.
Testimony is to continue all week.
